title: Review Record
body:
Each record contains `pull_request` (the full GitHub URL), `head` and `base` (full commit SHAs), `url` (the published HTTPS record URL), `reviewer`, `reviewed_at`, `scope`, `criteria`, `validation` and `findings`. The scope describes the full integration diff and inspected callers; criteria and validation describe the evidence inspected and its results. The pull request body links the published record.

Each finding contains `description`, `severity` (`blocking` or `nonblocking`) and `disposition` (`open`, `fixed` or `deferred`). A fixed finding has an HTTPS `evidence` link; a deferred finding has an HTTPS `ticket` link. Blocking findings, and every finding on a hot-fix's delivering pull request, must be fixed and reviewed at the recorded head. Every finding has a completed disposition before handoff. A record on a hot-fix's delivering pull request also carries `base_ref`, the name of its base branch. A record is current while it names the pull request's head and base SHAs. One on a hot-fix's delivering pull request is current while it names its head SHA and its base branch: its reviewed change is the head against its target, which a target moving on leaves as it was and a retarget does not. The last record for the same revision is authoritative.

references.text: - It is marked ready for review only once its review cycle is complete: its current [agent review](agent-review.md#review-record) leaves every finding fixed.

An open initiative whose criteria are all ticked is In Review. An open epic whose criteria are all ticked is In Review only with current published [agent review evidence](agent-review.md#review-record); missing, stale or unresolved review evidence keeps it In Progress.

Write a JSON list containing the [Review Record](#review-record), with the full reviewed head and target SHAs, the `base_ref` a hot-fix's record carries, the scope actually inspected, findings and validation results. An empty findings list states that the review found no defect.
- Refresh both pull request tips immediately before ready, board and user-handoff actions. A tip change that invalidates [Review Record](#review-record) requires another review.

title: Diagrams
body:
Every overview carries one structural diagram and one functional diagram. A further diagram is carried when the change warrants it, and displaces prose rather than adding to it.

| Diagram | Notation | Shows | Carried |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Component | `flowchart` with subgraphs | The areas the change reaches and the dependencies between them | Always, as the structural diagram |
| Class | `classDiagram` | The types the change adds or alters, their members and their relations | In place of the component diagram when the change sits in one area and lands in its types |
| Sequence | `sequenceDiagram` | One flow's ordered interactions between components | Always, one per flow the change runs through, as the functional diagram |
| State | `stateDiagram-v2` | One subject's states and the transitions between them | When the change alters a lifecycle |
| Before and After | A pair in the notation of the structure they show | The arrangement the change replaces beside the one it establishes | When the change rearranges structure or reorders a flow |

Component node shapes: `[text]` a module, `[(text)]` a store, `[[text]]` a process boundary, `([text])` an actor.

references.text: - The diagrams must meet [Measured Structure](../artifacts/architecture-overview.md#measured-structure) and [Diagrams](../artifacts/architecture-overview.md#diagrams).

title: Measured Structure
body: A component diagram's areas and edges, and a sequence's step order, are the ones measured over the graph. A boundary taken from the directory layout, and a call order traced by hand, are each a defect.

title: One Concept Per Diagram
body: Five to ten elements. A diagram that needs more splits by concept, and relationships between areas carry it rather than the internals of one.

title: Highlight
body: An element the change adds or alters carries a distinct fill, and untouched context is grey. A name and its fill hold across every diagram in the overview.

title: Labelled Edges
body: Every edge names its interaction, and its direction is the direction data or control travels.

title: Collections
body: Items of one kind go in a bulleted list, never packed into a paragraph. Each opens with a bold lead naming the item, and its body is the line beneath.

title: What Changed
body: What Changed states the behaviour each area now has. The change-by-change listing is the pull request's Changes section, which the overview links rather than reproduces.

title: Reading Order
body: One numbered entry per file the reviewer opens, ordered so the change reads from its entry point outward to what it calls. Each entry links the file at the head commit and gives one line on why it comes there. A file the change touches incidentally is left out.

title: Length
body: About two hundred lines, diagrams counted.

title: Sections
body: Summary, Structure, Behaviour, What Changed and Reading Order are always present. Risks and Watch Points, and References, are deleted when they have nothing to say.

title: Status Changes
body:
An issue closed as completed is Done. Every board item whose issue is closed any other way is removed, whether or not an initiative, epic or task body cites it.

An open initiative whose criteria are all ticked is In Review. An open epic whose criteria are all ticked is In Review only with current published [agent review evidence](agent-review.md#review-record); missing, stale or unresolved review evidence keeps it In Progress.

An open epic with a criterion unticked is In Progress while it is [active](board-queue.md#epic-activity). An inactive one keeps Ready or Backlog; In Progress and In Review become Backlog, and one not yet on the board is added at Backlog.

An initiative is In Progress when an epic its Work Breakdown lists is In Progress or In Review. An epic that has left that table is not read. Otherwise the initiative keeps the Status it holds, In Review becoming In Progress, and one not yet on the board is added at Backlog, so completed work alone starts no initiative. Delivery does not move an initiative or epic between Ready and Backlog.

Only an initiative, an epic or a hot-fix stands In Review. An open task issue is In Progress while a delivery pull request, draft or ready, links it, and Done once that pull request merges into the epic base and the issue closes as completed. Every jurisdiction refuses a task set In Review.

A task whose row links a reserved planning folder is In Progress. A work-item file link alone leaves the row available. Dispatch writes are limited to In Progress for held tasks and epics, and In Review for completed epics; the shared DISPATCH jurisdiction refuses other statuses and removals.

Task readiness must meet [Task Eligibility](board-queue.md#task-eligibility). The caller supplies saved issue bodies and closure state.

A task gated on an [unresolvable dependency](board-queue.md#unresolvable-dependencies) keeps the Status it holds: the row waits on no delivery, so no status follows from its gate. The run names the row and the entry and exits nonzero, as every reader of that cell does.

references.text: - A closed hot-fix takes the status [Status Changes](board-delivery.md#status-changes) gives a closed issue.

- Apply [Record Dispatch Status](#record-dispatch-status "ƒ") with the epic as the review identity for In Review or the progress identity for In Progress, as [Review Selection](#review-selection) requests, meeting [Status Changes](#status-changes).

title: Priority Sets
body:
A parallel work map assigns a positive integer to each ranked initiative. Every initiative with the same number runs together as one set. One left unordered stays in Backlog.

The epics of one initiative carry their own sets. Every epic with the same number starts together, and a number is compared only with its siblings'.

A priority label is `priority:` and a positive integer. A larger number is higher, with no maximum. Two such labels on one issue count as the larger number.

references.text: - For `order`, the answer is the [parallel work map](../artifacts/board-queue.md#priority-sets): a positive integer on each listed initiative, or none left unordered.
- The labels are `type:hot-fix`, the `theme:*` label of the board it sits on, and the [priority label](board-queue.md#priority-sets) for priority 10.

title: Initiative Status
body:
- The highest priority set is In Progress, all together. The next set is Ready, all together. Lower sets stay in Backlog. When the highest set leaves In Progress, the Ready set moves to In Progress.
- An initiative in Backlog with no priority label stays there. An initiative in Ready with no priority label moves to Backlog, as [Backlog Cascade](#backlog-cascade) states.
- An initiative In Progress with no priority label needs a decision: a positive integer keeps it In Progress; none sends it to Backlog once its epics' work has completed.
- An initiative stays In Progress while an epic its Work Breakdown lists is [active](#epic-activity), [handed off](#epic-handoff) or In Review, even when a higher set has started, as Board Delivery holds it In Progress. The epic's integration pull request is not activity; the epic's In Review status is what holds the initiative while that pull request awaits its merge. The highest set moves to In Progress immediately. Once that work completes, a lower set moves to Ready if it is the next number, or Backlog if a number sits between it and the highest.
- An initiative confirmed unplanned follows the same wait, then moves to Backlog as [Backlog Cascade](#backlog-cascade) states.
- An initiative In Review or Done remains in that state.

title: Hot-fix Placement
body: Each hot-fix stands where its [Board Status](hotfix.md#board-status) places it.

title: Epic Status
body:
- On an initiative Ready or In Progress, an [active](#epic-activity) epic is In Progress even with open questions. A delivered task row alone is not activity.
- On that initiative, an inactive epic can start when every entry of its initiative row's Depends on cell is delivered, every prerequisite epic that row names is closed as completed, all of each prerequisite's bases have merged into their long-lived branches, and the epic's Open Questions section is empty.
- Of the epics that can start, those carrying the highest priority number are next and Ready, all together. The highest counts the epics already In Progress, so an epic of a lower number waits while a higher one runs.
- An epic with no priority label is never Ready, whatever its siblings' state, so one that can start stays in Backlog.
- Any other Ready or In Progress epic of that initiative moves to Backlog.
- An epic In Review or Done, or [handed off](#epic-handoff), remains in that state.
- A Ready epic of an initiative that is neither Ready nor In Progress moves to Backlog. An epic is Ready only on an initiative Ready or In Progress.
- An initiative kept In Progress only while its epics' work completes readies none of its epics: its active epics are In Progress, and its inactive epics in Ready or In Progress move to Backlog.

title: Backlog Cascade
body:
An initiative that moves to Backlog takes its unstarted epics with it, and each loses its assignees, as [Assignees](board.md#assignees) states. Board Delivery moves each Ready task issue of a Backlog epic to Backlog, as [Task Eligibility](#task-eligibility) states.

An epic that is [active](#epic-activity), [handed off](#epic-handoff) or In Review is not released. The queue prints a `reconcile` line naming it, and the initiative and every one of its epics stay where they stand until the user finishes or releases that work.

references.text: - An initiative in Backlog with no priority label stays there. An initiative in Ready with no priority label moves to Backlog, as [Backlog Cascade](#backlog-cascade) states.
- An initiative confirmed unplanned follows the same wait, then moves to Backlog as [Backlog Cascade](#backlog-cascade) states.

title: Epic Activity
body:
An open epic is active while it has task work under way, and Board Delivery reads it the same way:

- a task row links a reserved planning folder, as [Task Delivery](epic-issue-body.md#task-delivery) defines, or
- an open pull request whose title names the epic, `[Ixx:Eyy]`, is not the epic's integration pull request, whose head is the epic base `ixx/eyy/<branch>` and whose base is `<branch>`.

A delivered row, and the integration pull request, are not activity.

references.text: - An initiative stays In Progress while an epic its Work Breakdown lists is [active](#epic-activity), [handed off](#epic-handoff) or In Review, even when a higher set has started, as Board Delivery holds it In Progress. The epic's integration pull request is not activity; the epic's In Review status is what holds the initiative while that pull request awaits its merge. The highest set moves to In Progress immediately. Once that work completes, a lower set moves to Ready if it is the next number, or Backlog if a number sits between it and the highest.

An epic that is [active](#epic-activity), [handed off](#epic-handoff) or In Review is not released. The queue prints a `reconcile` line naming it, and the initiative and every one of its epics stay where they stand until the user finishes or releases that work.

An open epic with a criterion unticked is In Progress while it is [active](board-queue.md#epic-activity). An inactive one keeps Ready or Backlog; In Progress and In Review become Backlog, and one not yet on the board is added at Backlog.

Board Delivery places it In Review when its current agent review passes, and holds it In Progress while that review is missing or failing. title: Task Eligibility
body: A task is Ready only when its epic is Ready or In Progress and every row its Depends on cell names is delivered. A row naming another epic's row waits for that row's outputs, as [Producer Outputs](delivery-branches.md#producer-outputs) states, and the rows beside it wait for nothing it waits on. The queue reads no checkout, so an output in the consumer's own repository stays unverified here, and the delivery survey, which reads one, is where such a row is found available. The queue contains no task issue changes; task status comes from the supplied delivery state.

references.text: An initiative that moves to Backlog takes its unstarted epics with it, and each loses its assignees, as [Assignees](board.md#assignees) states. Board Delivery moves each Ready task issue of a Backlog epic to Backlog, as [Task Eligibility](#task-eligibility) states.

A Ready unit contains one unjoined row or all rows of a unit defined by [Joins](dependency-graph.md#joins). Every member must be free and undelivered and meet [Task Eligibility](#task-eligibility) under its epic's proposed status; row availability follows [Task Delivery](epic-issue-body.md#task-delivery). Units include rows with no linked work item. Status and assignee calls depend on priority and delivery state.
Task readiness must meet [Task Eligibility](board-queue.md#task-eligibility). The caller supplies saved issue bodies and closure state.

title: Ready Units
body: A Ready unit contains one unjoined row or all rows of a unit defined by [Joins](dependency-graph.md#joins). Every member must be free and undelivered and meet [Task Eligibility](#task-eligibility) under its epic's proposed status; row availability follows [Task Delivery](epic-issue-body.md#task-delivery). Units include rows with no linked work item. Status and assignee calls depend on priority and delivery state.

references.text: | `unit` | A unit must meet [Ready Units](#ready-units) and [Unit Consistency](lane.md#unit-consistency) | Its initiative, epic and task ids followed by its [Report Label](lane.md#report-label), for example `unit I01:E00:W01+W02: lane 2` |

title: Proposed Changes
body: The queue contains calls for Status and assignee changes to initiatives, epics and hot-fixes. Status changes are between Backlog, Ready and In Progress, and a hot-fix's change as its [Board Status](hotfix.md#board-status) gives it. The assignee is the login assigned to work from Ready. Call files occupy the supplied output directory, for example `board/`. They describe proposed changes, not confirmation of live board state.

title: Report Lines
body:
| Line | When It Is Printed | What It Names |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `order` | No open initiative has a priority label | The open initiatives, including any already In Progress, for a parallel work map |
| `ask` | An initiative is In Progress and has no priority label | That initiative, for a positive integer or none |
| `wait` | An initiative is held In Progress by an epic it lists that is active, handed off or In Review | That initiative, the open delivery pull requests, and each epic In Review, awaiting review or held by a session |
| `reconcile` | An initiative would return to Backlog while an epic of it is active, handed off or In Review | That initiative and each such epic, for the user to finish or release |
| `next` | An initiative is Ready or In Progress and has epics that are Ready | Those epics |
| `unit` | A unit must meet [Ready Units](#ready-units) and [Unit Consistency](lane.md#unit-consistency) | Its initiative, epic and task ids followed by its [Report Label](lane.md#report-label), for example `unit I01:E00:W01+W02: lane 2` |
| `invalid` | A task has an [assignment finding](lane.md#assignments), or a free unit fails [Unit Consistency](lane.md#unit-consistency) | Its affected rows and values; the invalid unit is not reported as Ready, and the run exits nonzero |
| `rank` | An open initiative has an open epic with no priority label that is not [handed off](#epic-handoff) | That initiative and each such epic, for the user to rank |

title: Recommended Decisions
body:
The answer a caller applies where it resolves an `order` or `ask` line on its own.

- For `order`, priority 1 on every open initiative already In Progress or named by an open pull request, and no number on the rest. Where no initiative qualifies, nothing is under way and the line has no recommended answer.
- For `ask`, the number of the highest set already running, so the initiative joins it, or 1 where no initiative carries a priority label.

references.text: - For an automatic line, take its [recommended decision](../artifacts/board-queue.md#recommended-decisions) and Apply [Record Plan Change](../artifacts/plan-change.md#record-plan-change "ƒ") with that decision.

title: Unresolvable Dependencies
body:
A `Depends on` entry that names no row and links no issue, names an issue the run was not given, or names a row the epic it points to does not carry, cannot resolve. No delivery makes it readable, so it is told apart from a prerequisite that has not landed.

- The report names the row and the entry as written, and a run that met one while deciding a placement exits nonzero.
- The epic that row gates keeps the Status it holds. The run proposes no move for it, so a Ready epic stays Ready on an entry nobody can read.
- Every entry of a cell is read, so a cell carrying two names both.

references.text: Print proposed Status and assignee calls, [report lines](#report-lines) and unresolved issue references for one board queue and provide [Queue Result](#queue-result "●") to the requester. It exits nonzero for invalid task-table lane assignments or where an [unresolvable dependency](#unresolvable-dependencies) stopped it placing a row.

A task gated on an [unresolvable dependency](board-queue.md#unresolvable-dependencies) keeps the Status it holds: the row waits on no delivery, so no status follows from its gate. The run names the row and the entry and exits nonzero, as every reader of that cell does.

title: Completeness
body:
An `order` or `ask` line means a decision is pending. An unresolved issue reference means dependency evidence is missing. Either leaves the queue incomplete.

Invalid lane assignments leave the unit report incomplete and the run exits nonzero. They do not supply placement or assignee inputs.

A complete queue may still propose changes. Live board state has converged when a queue derived from refreshed items is complete and contains no further call. Every other [report line](#report-lines) remains reportable at that point.

title: Proposals
body:
- The [configured board](../configuration.md#proposals-board) holds proposal issues, the incoming funnel for work that may become an initiative.
- **Suggested.**
  Raised, and nobody has taken it up. A new proposal lands here, with no assignee.
- **Considering.**
  Someone is weighing the goal, the evidence and the criteria. That person is the assignee.
- **Approved.**
  Qualified to become an initiative. The assignee is the user.
- **Held.**
  Not now. It stays on the board, with no assignee.
- **Declined.**
  It will not become an initiative. It has no assignee.

title: Producer Outputs
body:
A task row naming another epic's row starts once that row is delivered and each output it delivered is available at the consumer's base commit.

- **The output.**
  Each merged pull request the producer row links carries its merge commit, on the long-lived branch its base names. Each commit the row links is an output of its own.
- **Available.**
  The output is an ancestor of the consumer epic's base on that branch, as the remote holds it at the evaluated commit, or of the long-lived branch itself while the consumer has no base there. An output another repository holds is available once it has reached its long-lived branch: delivered there, or carried by an integration pull request merged after it.
- **Not available.**
  A merge into the producer's own base alone, a merge into a ref that is neither an epic base nor a long-lived branch, such as a task branch, an output recording no merge commit, a commit the checkout does not hold, and a consumer base moved to a commit without the output each leave the row waiting.
- **Not gates.**
  The producer epic's other rows and its closure.
- **Record.**
  Each reading names the producer row, the delivery, the output commit, the consumer revision and commit, and the answer. The integration, review and human-approval gates on each epic stand apart from it.
- eg `#944 W02: E00:W01 #9 3f2a1c0d9b1e available at origin/i07/e01/main 8c4d2e7a1f30`.

references.text: A task is Ready only when its epic is Ready or In Progress and every row its Depends on cell names is delivered. A row naming another epic's row waits for that row's outputs, as [Producer Outputs](delivery-branches.md#producer-outputs) states, and the rows beside it wait for nothing it waits on. The queue reads no checkout, so an output in the consumer's own repository stays unverified here, and the delivery survey, which reads one, is where such a row is found available. The queue contains no task issue changes; task status comes from the supplied delivery state.

The dependent row starts once the producing row is delivered and its outputs are available at the dependent epic's base, as [Producer Outputs](delivery-branches.md#producer-outputs) states; the producing epic's other rows and its closure gate nothing.

- An `output` line records each output read for a row naming another epic's row, as [Producer Outputs](delivery-branches.md#producer-outputs) states: the producer row, the delivery, the output commit, the consumer revision and commit, and whether it is available there, or why it is unverified.

- **Changed branches.**
  A unit changes the long-lived branches its rows' work items name in their [Component](work-item.md#component) declarations. A unit of an epic with one base changes that base.
- **Unplanned rows.**
  A free row linking no work item is unplanned: its session writes the work item after dispatch. Its unit changes every epic base, and the session opens a pull request only from each branch its work changes.
- **Several long-lived branches.**

- **Hot-fix.**
  A hot-fix works on the branch its [Branch](hotfix.md#branch) names.

Each worktree is named by its branch under the worktree directory of the repository's main working tree.

title: Stash Entries
body:
Every worktree of a repository shares one stash list, so a delivery session that stashes names its entry with a message no other session's entry carries, and acts on that entry alone.

- **Found.**
  An entry is found by its message, never by its position in the list.
- **Restored.**
  An entry is restored with `git stash apply` on that entry's commit, never with a bare `git stash pop`, which takes whichever entry tops the list.
- **Dropped.**
  The session that made an entry drops it once restored, by the `stash@{<n>}` reference its message holds at that moment, since `git stash drop` takes no bare commit.
- eg `git stash push -m "i11/e10/w29 before base merge"`, then `git stash list --format='%H %gd %s'` to find the entry, `git stash apply <entry-commit>`, and `git stash drop "stash@{<n>}"`.

title: Report Lines
body:
- A `unit` line names one session's tasks, its lane as `lane 2` or `unlaned`, Coverage and record folder, then a branch, base and worktree for each epic base it changes, separated by semicolons: `branch i07/e00/w01-queue-plan-main, base i07/e00/main, worktree .worktrees/i07/e00/w01-queue-plan-main; branch i07/e00/w01-queue-plan-workflows, base i07/e00/workflows, worktree .worktrees/i07/e00/w01-queue-plan-workflows`. One base keeps the unsuffixed branch: `branch i07/e00/w01-queue-plan, base i07/e00/main, worktree .worktrees/i07/e00/w01-queue-plan`. A hot-fix's line names its prefix and issue: `unit F00 #874: unlaned, coverage AC1, record 2026-10-06-874-f00-key-validation, branch f00-key-validation, base workspace, worktree .worktrees/f00-key-validation`.
- An `invalid` line names a malformed task-table Lane cell or a joined unit with different Lane values. The unit is not offered and the run exits nonzero; the summary counts invalid units.
- An `undeclared` line names a row of a unit in an epic of several bases whose linked work item names no long-lived branch with an epic base, and why: the file is unread, or its component names no long-lived branch or one with no epic base. The unit is not offered until its work item declares one, and a run meeting one exits nonzero. It also names an open hot-fix, whatever its state, whose body names no [target](hotfix-body.md#target), or one of the project checkout's repository whose target the evaluated revision's [Branches](delivery-branches.md#branches) does not declare. It is offered as no unit and no merge until its target is one.
- A `hold` line names a row a session holds and the record it links, or a hot-fix its [Delivery Unit](hotfix.md#delivery-unit) holds.
- A `blocked` line names a free row whose dependencies are undelivered or whose joined task is unavailable.
- An `output` line records each output read for a row naming another epic's row, as [Producer Outputs](delivery-branches.md#producer-outputs) states: the producer row, the delivery, the output commit, the consumer revision and commit, and whether it is available there, or why it is unverified.
- An `unresolvable` line names a free row carrying a `Depends on` entry nothing can resolve, and the entry as written. The row waits on no delivery, so it is told apart from a blocked one, and a run meeting one exits nonzero.
- A `merge` line names an open pull request, never a draft, whose test plan has passed and the base it targets: a task pull request into an epic base, or an open hot-fix's [delivering pull request](hotfix.md#delivering-pull-request) into its target, when no `undeclared` or unresolved line names that hot-fix's target.
- An `unrecorded` line names a hot-fix its [Delivery Unit](hotfix.md#delivery-unit) leaves unrecorded, and each merged delivering pull request.
- An unresolved issue reference identifies missing dependency evidence.
- An unresolved hot-fix of a repository other than the project checkout's names its target, which that checkout's [Branches](delivery-branches.md#branches) cannot declare. It is offered once a plan whose project checkout is of its repository finds the target declared.

title: Edges
body:
A task edge names the producing row for each output the depending row consumes. An edge a task's prose implies is carried explicitly.

- **An edge names rows, never an epic.**
  A row naming an epic gates its task on every row of that epic, including the rows it consumes nothing from, which is how a [whole-epic edge](#whole-epic-edges) the rows do not justify reaches the initiative.
- **A task consuming from every row of an epic names the producing row for each output.**
  An edge another in the cell already implies is dropped, so a prerequisite chain is named by its last row, and the whole-epic reach is what the rows establish either way.
- **An edge to another epic's row waits for that row's outputs.**
  The dependent row starts once the producing row is delivered and its outputs are available at the dependent epic's base, as [Producer Outputs](delivery-branches.md#producer-outputs) states; the producing epic's other rows and its closure gate nothing.
- **An entry that cannot resolve is a permanent condition, not a prerequisite to come.**
  An entry naming no row and linking no issue, naming an issue the run was not given, or naming a row the epic it points to does not carry, cannot resolve. Every tool reading the cell names the entry as written, leaves the row where it stands rather than placing it as work still to come, and exits nonzero.

references.text: - Name the producing row for each consumed output, meeting [Edges](#edges), replacing an epic a task row names with the rows the task consumes.
- An entry it cannot resolve is a problem naming the entry as written, as [Edges](#edges) states. Its second clause says what this run could not find, which is the epics it was given.

- A task row naming an epic rather than the rows it consumes is a problem, as [Edges](#edges) states. That row still reaches the epic's rows, so a body carrying the retired form is reported once rather than taking its initiative's gates down with it.

title: Whole-Epic Edges
body:
An initiative Depends on cell takes the epics it derives, as [Work Breakdown](initiative-issue-body.md#work-breakdown) states. It derives one only where every row of the dependent epic requires every row of the prerequisite, through the task edges alone: a task row names rows, so no cell can assert a whole epic that the rows do not already establish.

- **The edge is the coarsest gate the plan has.**
  It holds the dependent epic until the prerequisite closes, not until the row it consumes merges, and it drops the dependent a [priority](#epic-priority) number, so the board keeps it out of Ready while the prerequisite runs.
- **Its cost is why it is derived and never written.**
  A narrower dependency stays in the task graph, where it gates the row that consumes the output rather than the epic around it.

references.text: A row naming an epic gates its task on every row of that epic, including the rows it consumes nothing from, which is how a [whole-epic edge](#whole-epic-edges) the rows do not justify reaches the initiative.

title: Epic Priority
body:
The map proposes one positive integer for each epic supplied, derived from the whole-epic edges and the components its rows declare. Epics sharing a number start together, so the number asserts they can run in parallel, and it holds a set only where both of these do.

- **Prerequisite depth establishes when an epic may start.**
  An epic with no prerequisite epic, one whose tasks are not yet written among them, carries the largest number, and each other epic takes one less than the smallest its prerequisites carry.
- **Component contention establishes whether it can.**
  An epic holding a row that contends with a row of an epic of the same depth takes the number below that depth, and the epics depending on it follow it down, as [Component Contention](#component-contention) states.

title: Component Contention
body:
Two task rows in different epics whose work items declare one [component](work-item.md#component) contend. Concurrent epics are two bases and two pull requests, so one component written from both is a merge conflict.

- Rows of one epic are out of scope: they land on one base, in the order Depends on and [Joins](#joins) set, so one component written twice is a rebase on that base rather than a conflict between two of them. [Joins](#joins) proposes them as one unit.
- A contending pair is answered by the number that separates its epics, or by moving the rows into one epic.

title: Joins
body:
The undelivered rows of one epic whose work items declare one [component](work-item.md#component) are a candidate unit: one pull request writes that file once, where separate ones each rebase on the last. Rows declaring different components need no accounting.

- **A joined unit has one lane.**
  Joined rows must meet [Unit Consistency](lane.md#unit-consistency).
- **A candidate is answered once.**
  Its rows name each other in Joins, or one line of a record names exactly its rows and why they stay split. A line naming only some of its rows, or rows besides, accounts for none.
- **Both resolutions are stated where the candidate is reported.**
  Naming the rows in Joins asserts one pull request; the record line says why there are several. A report naming only the first makes the assertion the cheaper answer.
- **A direct edge inside a candidate is the edge a join drops.**
  The report names it, since the joined pull request orders the commits.
- **Some candidates are split by rule.**
  A candidate whose rows cover more than six criteria, or with a path between two of them through a row outside it, cannot join. The report names the reason, and no record line is asked for.

Every member must be free and undelivered and meet [Task Eligibility](#task-eligibility) under its epic's proposed status; row availability follows [Task Delivery](epic-issue-body.md#task-delivery). Units include rows with no linked work item. Status and assignee calls depend on priority and delivery state.

title: Work Breakdown
body:
New tasks exist as epic rows with their details, discussion and evidence in the epic and planning record. Planning creates no separate task issues. Existing issues hoisted into an epic retain their records and row links when new tasks are planned.

The columns are `Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Lane | Done`.

- **Done.**
  A task row is complete when it is delivered, and every criterion its Coverage names is ticked.
- **Row id.**
  The row id is the task, `W01`. `W00` holds preparatory work that must land before the first real task.
- **Description.**
  Each detail beyond the phrase is a criterion stating one invariant.
- **Coverage.**
  Coverage names the epic's criteria the task delivers, whether its Done cell is ticked or empty. Each row claims only criteria its work makes true; it cannot claim a criterion another row delivers alone or one its work cannot meet. A cell is empty only on a delivered task whose criteria a further task adopts, as task grain states.
- **Depends on.**
  A task row names the rows it depends on. An earlier task in the epic (`W03`, `W04–W09`), a row of an earlier epic (`[E01:W02](…)`), or something outside the initiative (`#750`, `[I05:E00:W02](…)`).
  - A task row names rows, never an epic. It names the row producing each output it consumes (`[E01:W01](…), [E01:W02](…)`), and where the task consumes from every row of an epic that is what establishes the whole-epic reach.
  - Cross-epic dependencies name rows before any issue of the epic is created. Both tables exist, and each edge names the row that produces what the dependent row consumes.
  - A dependency listed twice or already implied by another in the cell is unsound. A task that measures, extends or consumes another task's output depends on it, even when the prose does not say so.
- **Task grain.**
  - A task is one pull request's worth of work.
  - A criterion a merged pull request left unticked belongs to a further task. The further task depends on the delivered task, and its Coverage is that criterion. Criteria one pull request can deliver share one further task. The delivered task's Coverage omits each criterion a further task adopts.
  - A task delivering more than three criteria is split into tasks one pull request each can deliver.
  - A task covers at least one acceptance criterion. A criterion more than one row cites is imprecise: it is split into the invariant each task makes true, and each is cited from the row that delivers it.
  - Every test the work calls for accompanies that task. The content steers which kinds those are, including the project's system test when the work is something that test can exercise. A failure in any test the task carries keeps the task open. None of those tests is a later row.
  - Reusable routines, techniques, and resources are specced, created, and tested before an activity binds them. The grain of an existing resource is in that work.
  - When the behaviour a wired activity produces differs from the behaviour the work expected, that task changes the routine, technique, or resource, and the tests that cover the change, until fit, form, and function hold.
- **Joins.**
  The tasks that share one pull request. Two tasks sharing one name each other, and tasks linked by such pairs are one joined unit.
  - A joined unit holds no Depends on between its members: the pull request orders their commits.
  - Only a path between two members through a task outside the unit bars a join.
  - A joined unit covers at most six criteria, two full rows' worth, so it stays one pull request's worth.
  - Joins are complete before any issue of the epic is created. Each candidate unit, the rows declaring one component, is answered as [Joins](dependency-graph.md#joins) states.
  - An empty cell is a task that shares no pull request.
- **Lane.**
  The row's delivery lane must meet [Assignments](lane.md#assignments).
- **Numbering.**
  Task numbering must meet [Numbering](issue-body.md#numbering); a row whose id links a pull request is fixed.
- **Reference form.**
  A table reference uses colons (`E01:W03`, `I05:E00:W02`), and every epic reference links to that epic's issue: `[E01:W03](…/issues/937)`. Prose uses a space (`E01 W03`).

title: Required Criteria
body:
A project states the criteria its epics must carry in `config/required-criteria.json` at its root. The file is a JSON array, and each entry is one required criterion with these fields, each a non-empty string except `paths`:

| Field | What it states |
| --- | --- |
| `branch` | The long-lived branch the criterion's work reaches. |
| `paths` | A non-empty list of files and directories on `branch`. An epic carries the criterion when a pull request of its work reaching `branch` changes a file that is one of them or lies under one. |
| `criterion` | The criterion's text, which the epic carries after its `**ACn.**` label. |
| `phrase` | A phrase identifying the criterion in an epic that carries it, matched without regard to case. |
| `row` | The Description of the task row that delivers the criterion. |

- **The declared row delivers the criterion.**
  It carries the declared `row` as its Description, depends on the rows whose work changes the declared paths, and covers that criterion alone.
- **The tracker states what the work changes.**
  The check reads each pull request's changed files as the tracker lists them. A pull request reaching the declared branch whose changed files are not supplied leaves the criterion unevaluable, unless another pull request of the epic is known to change a declared path.
- **The evaluated commit holds the statement.**
  The check reads the file at the commit its evaluated revision resolves to, in the repository its checkout locates, and names that path, commit and repository as its source. Which worktree the checkout is, and what its working files hold, choose nothing.
- **A project declaring nothing requires nothing.**
  A missing or empty file at the evaluated commit, or an empty array, declares no required criterion, and the check reports none. A project declaring nothing acquires no other project's criteria.
- **An unreadable statement is unevaluable.**
  A revision resolving to no commit, unreadable JSON, a value other than an array, or an entry lacking a field or stating `paths` as anything but a non-empty list of non-empty strings leaves the project's required criteria unevaluable. The check reports that and names the fault, and reports no epic as lacking a criterion.
- workflow-server requires its corpus audit of work that changes the workflow definitions under `corpus` on `workflows`: eg `[{"branch": "workflows", "paths": ["corpus"], "criterion": "The definitions this epic changes carry no outstanding confirmed finding, one neither fixed on the epic's branch nor taken by an issue, as the canon audit's coverage report shows.", "phrase": "canon audit", "row": "Canon audit of the changed definitions"}]`

references.text: For each epic pull request reaching a branch the project's [Required Criteria](#required-criteria) declare, Apply [Read Pull Request State](pull-request.md#read-pull-request-state "ƒ") to read its changed paths.

Include in the findings each [Required Criteria](#required-criteria) criterion an epic lacks whose work changes the criterion's paths on its branch, required criteria the declaration or the changed paths leave unevaluable, and any epic criterion no task row delivers.
- Confirm the epic carries every [Required Criteria](../artifacts/epic-issue-body.md#required-criteria) criterion its changes bring, with its declared delivering row.

title: Task Delivery
body:
- **Task ids.**
  - An unreserved task awaiting its pull request links its file in the planning record: `[W01](…/w01.md)`. The file name is the task id in lower case.
  - Every link on a task row names that row's id, and the row carries one delivery per long-lived branch its unit changes. A reserved task links only its planning folder: `[W01](…/2026-10-06-943-i07-e00-w01-queue-plan/)`. Every row of a joined unit links the one folder its first row names. The folder's README links each work-item file by the name the row's link carries. Releasing the reservation points the row to that file.
  - Once a pull request is open, its link replaces the planning link: `[W01](…/pull/950)`. A unit changing two long-lived branches links the pull request on each: `[W01](…/pull/950), [W01](…/pull/951)`. Further delivery work on one of those branches gets another task row under Task grain. Joined rows each link their shared pull request.
  - The task is delivered when a linked pull request has merged, or its id links a commit.
  - A link to an open pull request does not deliver the task.
  - A linked pull request whose title names another epic delivers the task once it has merged. The mismatch is reported, and the row stays open while a criterion its Coverage names is unticked.
- **Tasks with their own issue.**
  - A task issue belongs to one epic. Its title carries that epic's prefix.
  - When that epic's table has no row for its id, the issue is unplaced. Once the row exists, that epic's planning manages the issue.
  - The row links the pull request, not the issue.
  - The pull request's Development field links the issue as [Issue Links](pull-request.md#issue-links) state.
  - A completed task issue has all criteria verified and every Development-linked pull request merged.
- **Issues backing several tasks.**
  An issue backing several tasks, such as an investigation, is a reference: the epic cites it under References, no row id links it, and its title carries no agent-engineering prefix.
- **Work another issue takes.**
  It leaves the table. Its criteria go with it, or to another row that delivers them.

title: Delivery Findings
body:
| Line | What it names |
| --- | --- |
| Normalized | Closed-epic table corrections present in the output body. |
| Retitle | A merged pull request linked by a task row whose title has no prefix or only a matching initiative or task prefix, or any pull request whose title names an epic of the initiative by a task id, with the required title for publication and readback. |
| Conflict | Tasks that share a pull request and do not name each other in Joins. A row linked to a pull request whose title names another epic. |
| Unmatched | A merged pull request that names the epic and that no row links. |
| In flight | An open pull request that names the epic and that no row links. A pull request whose head is an epic base is not a task match. |
| Draft | An epic base a merged task targets that holds a commit its long-lived branch lacks and has no open pull request merging it, while a task is undelivered or a criterion is unticked. A base level with or behind its branch is not draft. |
| Unmerged | An epic base its pull requests target that has not merged into its long-lived branch, once every task is delivered and every criterion is ticked. A draft pull request is named draft. |
| References | A review pull request whose cited pull requests differ from the task pull requests merged into its base. |
| Changes | A review pull request whose Changes section names, in a code span, a file absent from the head commit of the base it fronts, with that span. A span, less any `#anchor` or `:line` suffix, names a path when it holds a directory and carries an extension or opens with a top-level directory of that head, or is a bare name whose extension a file at that head carries; a component `<branch>:<path>` names its path only for the base of that branch. A path stands where the head holds a file or a directory at it. |
| Uncited | A linked pull request whose task has its own issue and does not link it, or a review pull request that does not link the epic's issue. |
| Note | A row that links its task issue. |
| Unchanged | A row that links a task issue the run was not given. Its Done cell stands, and the epic is not closable until a run is given that issue. |
| Unplaced | A task issue of this epic whose id is not a row. |
| Open questions | The epic's Open Questions section remains. |
| Ready to verify | An unticked criterion whose delivering rows are all delivered and whose linked passed checks do not settle it. |
| Ticked early | A criterion ticked while a delivering row is not delivered. |
| Disagreement | A linked pull request's test plan against the Coverage of the rows it delivers. |
| Target | An open or merged pull request naming the epic off its delivery routes: a task pull request into anything but one of the epic's bases, or an integration pull request into anything but the long-lived branch its head names. Each names the base it belongs in: for a task pull request, the epic base of the long-lived branch its task branch's last slug word names where another of the epic's pull requests comes from a branch of the same stem ending in another long-lived branch, as a unit changing several takes one task branch per base; else of the one its target names; else each epic base as one of them. |
| No epic | A pull request whose title opens with the initiative's id, `[I07`, and names neither an epic as `[I07:E00]` nor a task as `[I07:E00:W01]`: a bare `[I07]`, or an epic id in any other form, such as `[I07:E1]`. Nothing reads it as delivery. |
| Source | The configuration path, commit and repository of each `config/branches` statement the long-lived branch names were read from. |
| Unevaluable | A `config/branches` statement that is absent, empty or unreadable at its epic base, or a revision resolving to no commit, with its source; statements that disagree across the epic bases, each with its source and names; no long-lived branches given; a base that would be draft whose commits cannot be compared with its long-lived branch; or a review whose head commit the checkout does not hold, so its Changes paths are unread; each with the reason. |
| Not checked | Each epic check that reads the long-lived branches, while their names are unevaluable. |

title: Work Breakdown
body:
The columns are `Epic | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Done`. The table has no Joins column.

- An epic row's id is the epic, linked to its issue: `[E01](…/issues/937)`.
- An epic row's Description is the epic's title name, and its Coverage names the initiative criteria the epic serves.
- An epic row is complete when its issue is closed as completed.
- An epic row whose issue is closed as not planned leaves the table. Each criterion only that row covers leaves with it, and a criterion another row also covers stays. The criteria that remain keep their [labels](issue-body.md#criterion-labels).
- Depends on names epics only. A cell that names a task fails. Name a prerequisite epic only when every task or joined unit in the dependent epic requires every task in that prerequisite epic, directly or through its dependencies. The consumed output and the work producing it establish that requirement. Dependencies on selected tasks remain in the task tables. An edge another named whole-epic prerequisite already implies is omitted.
- An initiative dependency that only some tasks need, or that requires only part of its prerequisite epic, is overbroad. The output and its producing tasks establish the edge.
- An epic depending on a later epic is a backward reference.
- Epic numbering must meet [Numbering](issue-body.md#numbering).

references.text: - Each row must meet [Work Breakdown](#work-breakdown).
Apply the initiative's [whole-epic dependency rule](initiative-issue-body.md#work-breakdown); a task row's reference to a row of another epic gates that row rather than this epic.
- Initiative edges must follow the [whole-epic prerequisite rule](initiative-issue-body.md#work-breakdown); narrower dependencies stay in the task graph.

An initiative Depends on cell takes the epics it derives, as [Work Breakdown](initiative-issue-body.md#work-breakdown) states. It derives one only where every row of the dependent epic requires every row of the prerequisite, through the task edges alone: a task row names rows, so no cell can assert a whole epic that the rows do not already establish.

title: Initiative Acceptance Criteria
body:
An initiative criterion must meet the [shared acceptance criteria](issue-body.md#shared-acceptance-criteria) and [Requirement Characteristics](../references/requirement-characteristics.md), and:

- **No counts.**
  An initiative criterion carries no counts or figures, which go stale: it measures against a named baseline or check ("against the baseline", "as the budget test measures it"). A figure stays only where it is the criterion's own target, such as a bound it holds to.
- **SMART.**
  Each initiative criterion is specific about what holds, measurable by a named check or baseline, achievable by the epics that cite it, and relevant, tracing to a clause and to the Problem. It is time-bound by a release tag or another named milestone outside the initiative's own work, where one exists, and otherwise by the epics that cite it.
- **Local.**
  An initiative criterion names no initiative, epic, task or issue, and is solution-agnostic. Coverage cells link epics to criteria. One that holds only through another initiative's work is restated as what this initiative achieves, or it is dropped.
- **Whole.**
  An initiative criterion states what the initiative achieves as a whole. One that restates a single epic's criterion is a duplicate: it is raised to what the epics achieve together, or left to the epic.
- **Verified.**
  - An initiative criterion ends by naming its instrument. Which instruments keep a criterion is [Verifiable](issue-body.md#verifiable).
  - An automated test is an end-to-end walk through the real server, a smoke run of an agent against a live server, a live check on a deployed host, or a guard, fixture suite or check that continuous integration runs. The walk, smoke run or live check is preferred where the criterion is about what a run does.
  - A named test that does not exist yet is work the plan holds: a task in the epic whose subject it tests, or a discrete test-infrastructure epic when the tests serve several criteria. That epic's row cites the criteria its tests verify.

references.text: - An acceptance criterion is created only once it meets [Initiative Acceptance Criteria](../artifacts/initiative-issue-body.md#initiative-acceptance-criteria).
- Each criterion must come from a confirmed clause and meet [Initiative Acceptance Criteria](#initiative-acceptance-criteria).

title: Titles
body:
- **Titles.**
  - A title is a short name, a colon, and a subtitle stating the outcome.
  - The name is two or three words and the subtitle a succinct summary of at most ten, in title case.
  - A prefixed title separates its levels with colons, then the name.
- **Bodies.**
  - Every body keeps the section order of its kind template and the columns of that kind's table.
  - Fill each `{{…}}` and delete a section the template marks as optional when it has nothing to say.
- **Code references.**
  A body references code as a link on the words it supports, a permalink pinned to a commit with its line anchors, never a bare `path:line`: `the [extrinsic type](…/blob/<sha>/runtime/src/lib.rs#L1231-L1232)`.
- **Succinct items.**
  Each Problem and Proposal item, and each of its sub-bullets, is at most two lines. A bold opener does not count toward the two. Several distinct points go in a bulleted list, never packed into those two lines.
- **Bold leads.**
  - A Problem or Proposal item that opens with a bold statement puts its body on the next line, indented under the bullet:

    ```markdown
    - **Length is the only check on entry.**
      The data source decodes the key and never checks its value.
    ```

  - A bulleted item with sub-bullets keeps the line introducing them on its bold statement's line:

    ```markdown
    - **Framing is undocumented.** Nothing describes:
      - the runtime's extrinsic type;
    ```
- **Labels.**
  - Add `enhancement`, `bug` and `tech-debt` as they apply.
  - eg `workflows` for workflow-server.
  - Only labels that exist are applied.

title: Shared Acceptance Criteria
body:
An acceptance criterion must meet these. A kind adds its own under its Acceptance Criteria.

- States an end state, not an activity.
- Names or implies the instrument that observes it: a test, a guard, a command or a measure.
- Is unambiguous, so two readers agree on whether it holds.
- Meets [Requirement Characteristics](../references/requirement-characteristics.md).
- **One invariant.**
  Each criterion states a single condition that holds or does not. One joining several is split, and the Coverage cells cite the new ones. A condition over a list of subjects is one condition.

#### Criterion Labels

Criteria are labelled `AC1` onward, in ascending order. A criterion that leaves a body takes its label with it, and the criteria that remain keep theirs, since other work cites them, so the labels may ascend with a gap.

#### Verifiable

- Subjective wording is an observable pass or fail, or the criterion is absent.
- A fact that inspection, analysis, demonstration, or test can check is kept, such as every option having a description.
- A judgment about meaning, such as a claim that a description states what choosing means, is subjective wording.
- An item none of those methods can observe is named as [Coverage Reports](#coverage-reports) define, and it stays named there.

references.text: - A task criterion must meet the [shared acceptance criteria](issue-body.md#shared-acceptance-criteria).
An initiative criterion must meet the [shared acceptance criteria](issue-body.md#shared-acceptance-criteria) and [Requirement Characteristics](../references/requirement-characteristics.md), and:
An epic criterion must meet the [shared acceptance criteria](issue-body.md#shared-acceptance-criteria). Contradictions between criteria in one epic are findings.
- The body must meet [Body](#body), [Shared Acceptance Criteria](#shared-acceptance-criteria) and the supplied [kind conditions](#kind-conditions).
Check each criterion against the [shared acceptance criteria](issue-body.md#shared-acceptance-criteria) and [Initiative Acceptance Criteria](initiative-issue-body.md#initiative-acceptance-criteria).

  The acceptance criteria the row delivers, `AC2, AC5`, and nothing else. Every criterion is delivered by at least one row.
- **Depends on.**
  References only, with no prose, and only what no other entry in the cell already implies.

title: Coverage Reports
body:
- **Unobservable items.**
  An item a test cannot observe is named in the plan or the coverage report. It stays in the report.
- **The check matches the criterion.**
  - A file or string check counts as coverage only when the criterion is a fact about that file.
  - A criterion about a run is covered by a run that shows it.
- **The specified set.**
  A coverage report lists every acceptance criterion the work under review is specified to cover.

- Report per issue: tasks linked, criteria ticked, rows marked done, criteria left unticked and why, conflicts, test plan disagreements, what was closed, each board and assignee change, and each overview written. What the report names about criteria is [Coverage Reports](../artifacts/issue-body.md#coverage-reports).
- An item a test cannot observe must stay named as [Coverage Reports](issue-body.md#coverage-reports) define.
- An item none of those methods can observe is named as [Coverage Reports](#coverage-reports) define, and it stays named there.

- Every criterion a unit's Coverage names has an observing test in its work item and pull request. A criterion no test can observe remains in the [coverage report](issue-body.md#coverage-reports) and in a test-plan row with an empty Test cell.

- The criterion selects the test kind: a unit test for one component, an integration test for a seam between components, and an end-to-end or system test for running-system behaviour. That evidence must meet [Coverage Reports](issue-body.md#coverage-reports).

A criterion is verified only on a passing run of its named instrument, recorded against the tested revisions as [Coverage Reports](issue-body.md#coverage-reports) define. A failed, unavailable or inconclusive instrument leaves it unverified, and an unverified criterion is not ticked.

title: Auto-Close Setting
body:
GitHub's **Auto-close issues with merged linked pull requests** repository setting, which must be disabled before a delivery pull request is linked or merged, so that closure follows the criteria rather than the merge.

- The setting is confirmed per repository and holds for the session; it is not inferred from an issue that stayed open.
- No REST field and no GraphQL field of `gh` 2.46 carries it, so on such a host the user's explicit answer is the only source.
- An enabled or unconfirmed setting blocks delivery links and merges until the setting is confirmed disabled. Changing the setting requires the user's explicit authorization.
- The setting gates the links and merges that precede closure; the closure gate takes no input from it.

references.text: Where no API field carries it, put the setting to the user and take their explicit answer, meeting [Auto-Close Setting](#auto-close-setting).
The caller’s repository auto-close setting confirmed for the session, meeting [Auto-Close Setting](issue.md#auto-close-setting).

title: Index
body: An index is an opaque board-wide decimal string. Its spelling is significant: `02` and `2` are distinct indices, and `0` is valid. The same index identifies one lane across the theme board.

references.text: - For an initiative using lanes, propose each task row's [Lane](../artifacts/lane.md#index) index as a map for the user to confirm, assigning joined rows together as [Unit Consistency](../artifacts/lane.md#unit-consistency) requires. Record the confirmed map in the planning record. For an initiative without lanes, leave the row lanes empty.

One run records its board identity, scope selectors and requested lane in a JSON object. The scope is the selected board (`["*"]`), or a list of repository-qualified initiative, epic, task or hot-fix identities, such as `o/r#I07`, `o/r#I07:E00`, `o/r#I07:E00:W01` or `o/r#F02`. Every row of a joined unit must fall within that scope. An explicit joined selector, `o/r#I07:E00:W01+W02`, authorizes both rows. The requested lane must meet [Index](lane.md#index), represented as `null` when none is requested. eg `{"board": "users/o/projectsV2/7", "scope": ["o/r#I07"], "lane": null}`

title: Titles
body:
- A pull request's title starts with the epic it works on: `[I07:E00] Purpose`.
- A hot-fix's pull request takes the title its [Delivering Pull Request](hotfix.md#delivering-pull-request) names.
- A pull request working on neither an epic nor a hot-fix takes `Name: Subtitle`, with no prefix, as a revision of the skill itself does.
- The prefix is how an epic's pull requests are found, and each one, open or merged, is matched to the tasks it works on from its changes and the tasks' Descriptions.
- The pull request that merges an epic base carries the same prefix. Its head is the epic base, which tells it from a task pull request.
- A title carrying an initiative's prefix names one of its epics. An epic sync reports one that names none as `no epic`, and one naming its epic by a task id, `[I07:E00:W01]`, as `retitle`.

title: Review Body
body:
- Overview is one paragraph on what the base carries.
- Changes holds one heading per area, with a bullet per functional change.
- A Changes bullet states what the base does and carries no count of the corpus, such as how many specifications or files it holds. A count belongs in the unit's planning record, with the revision that produced it.
- Each file a Changes bullet names in a code span stands at the base's head. A code name, such as `board.Outputs`, names no file.
- References cites each task pull request merged into that base.
- It carries no Test Plan, since it delivers no task of its own, and no statement about what the epic has yet to deliver. The epic's Work Breakdown is where delivery state is read.

title: Test Plan
body:
A task pull request carries a Test Plan.

- **Table.**
  The pull request's Test Plan section contains only one table, with columns Test, Description, Coverage and Pass, in that order.
- **Columns.**
  - Test names the id.
  - Description briefly names the check.
  - Coverage names the criteria the check observes, `AC1, AC3`, and is empty when the check observes none.
  - A row whose Test cell is empty names a criterion no check observes, and its Pass cell is empty.
  - Pass is empty while a check awaits a result. A recorded result uses ✓ when the check ran and held, or an accurate label such as Partial, Fail or Not run.
- **Evidence.**
  - Test procedures, tested revisions, observations, limitations and supporting evidence belong in the work's published planning document.
  - Each recorded result in Pass links to its relevant section in that document, using the result as link text: `[✓](URL#check)` or `[Partial](URL#check)`.
  - Each evidence link is accessible to the pull request's readers and resolves to the intended section.
- **Completion.**
  The test plan has passed when every row with a Test id carries ✓ as its result. Partial, failed and unexecuted checks remain incomplete.

title: Test Coverage
body:
- Every criterion a unit's Coverage names has an observing test in its work item and pull request. A criterion no test can observe remains in the [coverage report](issue-body.md#coverage-reports) and in a test-plan row with an empty Test cell.

- An instrument that does not exist yet is work the task carries, as the verified rule defines. Use the project's own system test where it can observe the criterion.
- One row per check, in execution order, followed by any unobserved criteria. Every criterion in the unit's Coverage appears in at least one row.

title: Merge Permission
body:
The agent harness lets a delivery session merge a task pull request into an [epic base](delivery-branches.md#epic-bases), such as `i07/e00/main`, without a prompt. A merge into the default branch stays with a person.

- **Claude Code.**
  User settings (`~/.claude/settings.json`) grant it with an `autoMode.allow` rule and an `autoMode.environment` entry, each array keeping `"$defaults"`; auto mode reads neither from project settings. `claude auto-mode config` prints the rules in effect. eg `{"autoMode": {"environment": ["$defaults", "Source control: github.com/m2ux/workflow-server. Epic bases named iNN/eNN/<branch> carry no review requirement; the default branch requires an approving review"], "allow": ["$defaults", "Merging a task pull request into an epic base iNN/eNN/<branch> of github.com/m2ux/workflow-server is allowed: the work-planner skill's Deliver mode authorizes it and the base requires no review. Merges into the default branch are not covered"]}}`

references.text: The agent harness grants the [Merge Permission](artifacts/pull-request.md#merge-permission) Deliver needs.

- If the agent's own permission layer refuses it, the harness declines to run the merge command and GitHub returns nothing. On a target with no review requirement, that refusal is neither a handoff for approval nor a branch blocker. Provide the pull request as ready and verified, naming the refusal and the [merge permission](#merge-permission) it lacks, and stop merge attempts. A later Deliver run merges it in its merge step or reports the missing permission; neither asks the user to approve it.
- Confirm the harness provides sub-agent dispatch and the [epic-base merge permission](../artifacts/pull-request.md#merge-permission); provide the absent capability before holding work.

title: Issue Links
body:
- GitHub shows the link in the pull request's Development field and in the issue's Linked pull requests field, which the project board reads.
- A task pull request links the task's issue, and a review pull request links its epic's issue.
- The link is addressed by issue, so a pull request whose work carries no issue links nothing. A task pull request delivering rows that have no issue of their own is the whole of what stays unlinked.
- The link is stored on the pull request. It holds on any base branch and on a pull request that has merged, and a later body edit leaves it standing.
- A linked issue remains open until its criteria and delivery requirements hold and every Development-linked pull request is merged.
- The field is the whole of the relation: neither body links the other. The pull request's References carry its sources, and the issue it delivers is not among them.
- A pull request with a delivery issue but no Development link is uncited.

title: Scope
body:
When no start date is supplied, the window follows [Standup Configuration](../configuration.md#standup). A supplied start date selects another window, such as the previous working day for a daily standup. An initiative filter names one initiative, qualified by repository when its number is ambiguous.

Each repository numbers its own initiatives, and an initiative's epics and task issues may live in other repositories. Each item's place follows the Work Breakdown links, or for a task issue the pull request whose Development field links it. A pull request counts towards the epic of its reference in the epic's repository or its initiative's.

title: Sections
body:
The management paragraph is set off by blank lines, with the board's link beneath the heading.

- **Initiatives.**
  One line for each initiative with work under Completed or In progress, its title's name and subtitle, opening with the mark of its state. One off the board is done when closed, else in progress. An item works for the initiative whose table links its epic and for the one its epic's title names.
- **Completed.**
  Items Done whose issue closed in the window, grouped under their epic, and tasks whose pull requests merged in it. Closing is when an issue became Done; an issue the board caught up with later still falls on its closing date.
- **In progress.**
  Epics In Progress or In Review and task issues In Progress, each epic with its open pull requests, or else its next task.
- **Next.**
  The five Ready items, each epic with its next task, and a count of the rest.
  - Ready hot-fixes lead.
  - They rank by the priority label of the initiative their epic belongs to, then by their epic's own.
  - An epic is placed ahead of any listed epic naming it, so a supplier reads before the work drawing on it. An epic names another when a task row names one of its rows or the initiative row names it whole.
- **Hot-fixes.**
  Each [hot-fix](hotfix-body.md) follows the epic groups of Completed, In progress or Next as its status places it, with its [delivering pull requests](hotfix.md#delivering-pull-request) beneath. An initiative filter leaves hot-fixes out.
- **Key.**
  I Initiative, E Epic, W Work Item and F Hot-fix. Opening marks are ✅ done, 🔄 in progress (an initiative, epic or hot-fix open and not In Review, or a task issue In Progress), 👀 in review (an initiative, epic or hot-fix In Review, or a pull request ready for review), 📝 draft and ▶️ ready.

title: Component
body:
One declaration line ahead of the first heading, naming the single component the Implementation part extends as `<long-lived branch>:<path>`: the [long-lived branch](delivery-branches.md#branches) that holds it and the path to it there, such as `workspace:skills/work-planner/scripts/deliver.py`.

- A task that creates the component names the path it creates.
- The long-lived branch decides which of an epic's bases the task's unit changes, as [Task Branches](delivery-branches.md#task-branches) states.
- A task whose implementation extends more than one component is split into a task for each.
- A component is one file, never a directory, since the dependency check groups an epic's rows into candidate units by it.

references.text: - Confirm the base it names against its work item's [Component](../artifacts/work-item.md#component): the confirmed base is the epic base of the long-lived branch that Component names, whether the finding names that base, another, or one of several.
- The supplied component must meet [Component](#component).
- Component names the component the Implementation part extends, meeting [Component](#component).
A unit changes the long-lived branches its rows' work items name in their [Component](work-item.md#component) declarations. A unit of an epic with one base changes that base.

Two task rows in different epics whose work items declare one [component](work-item.md#component) contend. Concurrent epics are two bases and two pull requests, so one component written from both is a merge conflict.

The undelivered rows of one epic whose work items declare one [component](work-item.md#component) are a candidate unit: one pull request writes that file once, where separate ones each rebase on the last. Rows declaring different components need no accounting.

A unit is one task row or tasks that name each other in Joins, as [Work Breakdown](epic-issue-body.md#work-breakdown) defines. A unit of rows comes only from an epic that is Ready or In Progress in the supplied board items: the plan offers no other row, and none other is held. A [hot-fix unit](#hot-fix-units) has no row. One unit is one session's work, delivered by one pull request into each epic base it changes. Its first task id and Description determine the planning-folder identity, which every row of the unit is reserved with, and with each epic base it changes its branch and worktree, as [Task Branches](delivery-branches.md#task-branches) names them. In an epic of several bases, the bases a unit changes are read from the [Component](work-item.md#component) declaration of the work-item file each free row links, in the engineering worktree. A unit with a row linking no work item changes every epic base, as [Task Branches](delivery-branches.md#task-branches) states for unplanned rows.
